verdict.headline: Oil regime threshold crossed on Iran escalation as PMI boom masks second straight weekly loss
verdict.label: Brent $94.39 — regime trigger active; composite PMI 56.0 (4-year high) lifts Friday; S&P −1.4% weekly; 30Y 5bps from 5.30% trigger; VIX +7.5% on green day
verdict.rationale_short: Brent closed at $94.39, crossing the formal regime threshold the morning brief identified as the level that changes the chip-sector setup, driven by Trump's 'economic D-Day' Iran escalation — Bessent details the plan Monday. A flash composite PMI of 56.0 (the fastest US business growth since April 2022, services 56.8 vs. 54.0 estimate) explained the day's small equity gains but did not reverse two back-to-back weekly losses. With oil now through the threshold and 30Y at 5.25% (5bps from the 5.30% formal trigger), the setup heading into NVDA's Aug 26 print is materially more asymmetric than Thursday; the level that would contain it is Brent retreating below $93 on credible Iran de-escalation before the print.

trade_setups.asset: Brent crude — first formal breach; Bessent press conference Monday
trade_setups.thesis: Brent closed at $94.39, crossing the formal $94 regime trigger for the first time. Trump's 'economic D-Day' Iran escalation (secondary sanctions on nations trading with Tehran) is the proximate driver; Bessent details specifics Monday Aug 24. Iranian President Pezeshkian's de-escalation language is the counter — the first substantive signal from Tehran since the conflict began — but no formal negotiating channel has opened. PMI manufacturing supply-chain stress and shipping disruptions add structural oil supply uncertainty independent of the geopolitical catalyst.
trade_setups.entry: The breach level is $94; $93 is the threshold where de-escalation begins pricing in. Above $96 historically elevates risk premia across long-duration assets and compresses growth-sector multiples.
trade_setups.invalidation: Credible Iran de-escalation or formal diplomatic channel announced before Monday's Bessent press conference. Brent closing below $93 on two consecutive sessions.
trade_setups.horizon: 72 hours to Monday close; definitively resolved by NVDA print Aug 26

trade_setups.asset: 30Y Treasury — 5bps from completing the two-indicator configuration
trade_setups.thesis: The two-indicator stagflation framework activates when Brent >$94 AND 30Y >5.30% simultaneously. Brent is now active. 30Y at 5.25% is 5bps from the second trigger. Bifurcated PMI — services running hot, manufacturing supply-chain stress extending — is the precise configuration that keeps the Fed's rate path uncertain and the long end supply-driven. No scheduled macro data before Monday's Bessent press conference; direction will follow oil and any long-end auction dynamics.
trade_setups.entry: 5.25% current; 5.30% is the formal trigger for the full stagflation configuration. 5.20% is the level where the Bessent buyback supply-signal begins pricing in early.
trade_setups.invalidation: Bessent's Monday statement anchors oil supply expectations, Brent retreats below $93, and 30Y pulls back below 5.20%. A soft macro surprise compressing September hike odds materially below 25%.
trade_setups.horizon: Monday close; Aug 26 NVDA print; Jackson Hole Aug 28 Warsh keynote

trade_setups.asset: AMD — seven sessions below $484; first recovery move
trade_setups.thesis: AMD gained 1.4% to close at $473.25 Friday — the first meaningful recovery in the seven-session streak below $484 containment. $484 functions as the chip-sector leading indicator heading into NVDA's Aug 26 print: below it signals multiple exhaustion at sector altitude; above it on two consecutive closes would signal a sentiment reset. The BABA AI cloud +45% demand read-through argues fundamentals are intact; the seven-session containment failure argues multiple compression is the dominant market read regardless of demand.
trade_setups.entry: AMD at $473.25; $484 is the containment level that changes the sector configuration. $450 is the negative confirmation level if the recovery reverses before NVDA's print.
trade_setups.invalidation: AMD closes above $484 on Tuesday and Wednesday before the NVDA print, or NVDA delivers gross margin >78% AND data-center guide >$39B — both conditions simultaneously — which would revalue the sector independent of AMD's current position.
trade_setups.horizon: Tuesday Aug 25 and Wednesday Aug 26 close before NVDA reports

bear_case: The Brent regime trigger has fired — the same configuration that framed the August 7 NFP shock. Bessent's Monday 'Operation Economic Fury' press conference adds to supply disruption risk rather than resolving it. 30Y at 5.25% is 5bps from activating the rate leg of the two-indicator stagflation configuration. Bifurcated PMI (services 56.8 vs. manufacturing supply-chain stress at a 13-month output low) argues the Fed cannot cut in September, which keeps the long end supply-driven. VIX at 16.01 rising on a green Friday is the most direct market signal: options desks are buying protection for the NVDA print and Warsh keynote that equity cash has not yet priced. The level that flips this: Brent back below $93 AND 30Y back below 5.20%, both within 48 hours of Monday's open.
